author: madwt
text:
Hi Madwt, The reason i thought demand is consumed is as shown on the chart and the momentum bar is due to overhead supply being removed creating liquidity gap(?)

I think if you keep studying CP you will look back at your chart later and see that it's not a great example of CP. Price did slice back through the area, though I suspect for a different reason. You are correct that the candle tails shown are consuming demand at that level, though there is still some unconsumed demand (albeit, not great demand) below those candle tails. It's not a 'good' one, but what I have marked is a DBR. As such, there is a chance of price will react when it comes back.

Good CP, the ones you are looking to exploit leave no (or very little) unconsumed demand on the move up.

Have a look at the post by In2Forex above as an example. It may help.

Hi MW,

If I understand your question correctly, CPed PA can indeed form Supply or Demand.... Take a look at the education section of this site, under price reading, and see what you find there. In my opinion price can form a base be it supply or demand and either leave this base with high momentum or with CPed motion, but a question you have to ask yourself is who was active at that time, would that zone be worth taking a FTB??

I have drawn a quick example up for you, however a word of caution, CPed action from a demand or supply may mean accumulation, this indicates the ITs gathering orders for the move up or down....
